summary: Build practical AI governance skills with NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001. Learn policy, controls, risk registers, and reporting.
lede: AI governance training helps professionals responsible for oversight turn responsible AI principles into documented policies, controls, and review routines. It covers building an AI inventory and risk register, classifying use cases, mapping risks to controls, and setting ownership and approval checkpoints. Participants also practice lifecycle monitoring, bias and privacy reviews, and reporting risk, remediation, and exceptions.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who need to govern AI responsibly, document controls, and report risk with confidence.
prerequisites: You should have a working understanding of how your organization uses AI, data, analytics, or automated decision systems. No coding is required, but you will benefit from prior exposure to risk, compliance, data governance, product management, or technology oversight processes. Familiarity with basic AI concepts, model lifecycle stages, and internal approval workflows will help you complete the exercises more confidently. Advanced technical engineering of models is not required; the course focuses on operational application of AI governance, not machine learning development.
